newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seeks peace with rebels despite fighting.
newsitem.headline: Manila seeks peace with rebels despite fighting.

text.p: The Philippine government said on Friday it wanted to press on with peace negotiations with Moslem separatists in the south of the country after nearly two weeks of heavy fighting in which more than 45 people have died.

"We are not changing our policy. Our basic policy is that we will do our best to resolve the issue, the armed conflict, the fighting, through peaceful negotiations," Defence Secretary Renato De Villa said in a radio interview.
At least seven people died on Thursday in a gunbattle with Moslem rebels who were holding nearly 50 people hostage near Cotabato in the southern island of Mindanao.
The hostages were freed and more than 1,000 members of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) later fled their second largest base on the island.
The MILF, with an estimated 8,000 armed fighters, is battling for independence for Mindanao, the ancestral Moslem homeland in the predominantly Christian country.
It was not party to an agreement with the Philippine government late last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front, which had also been fighting for a separate state.
The latest fighting prompted the MILF to indefinitely postpone the exploratory peace talks with Manila which were scheduled for this weekend.
The military says at least 45 people have been killed since fighting erupted almost two weeks ago, and more than 20,000 villagers have fled their homes.

De Villa said while he was confident the 25-year old Moslem separatist insurrection could be resolved through peaceful negotiations, the latest fighting could not have been avoided while the rebels sowed terror in the countryside.
"If we are being attacked, we just can't stand there and accept the bullets being fired by the enemies," he said.
"We are not out to kill people. We are not out there to fight. We are going there to maintain the climate of peace," he added.
